items.q: Why doesn't every experience rewire an adult brain?
items.a: Neuroplasticity is lifelong, but after **~25** it is **gated**. Babies are crude wide webs; adults need a specific neurochemical state. *"The nervous system doesn't just change because you experience something unless you're a very young child."*

items.q: What opens plasticity to a specific experience?
items.a: Only experiences you **pay super careful attention to** open plasticity — and only to **that specific content**. Merzenich/Recanzone drum experiments: adult touch maps rewired **only when subjects attended to touch**, not when attention went to an auditory cue.

items.q: Which neurochemicals are required for adult brain change?
items.a: You need **epinephrine** (alertness) + **brainstem acetylcholine** (spotlight / signal-to-noise) + **nucleus basalis acetylcholine** (marks active circuits). When all three are present, *"you can change your brain… it absolutely will change."*

items.q: Is agitation during focus a bad sign?
items.a: No — **agitation and challenge while focusing** usually means **epinephrine is doing its job**. *"Chances are you're doing it right."* Nicotine can bind nicotinic ACh receptors, but Huberman warns against **chronic pharmacologic focus** — plasticity needs a **distinct window** from baseline.

items.q: What is step one before trying to change a behavior?
items.a: **Awareness / recognition**: name what you want to change — even telling someone your voice triggers them **begins plasticity**. Then build **alertness** via sleep mastery plus an accountability kit (love, fear, shame, public commitment all release **epinephrine equally**).

items.q: How does visual focus create mental focus?
items.a: *"Mental focus follows visual focus."* Hold a **narrow visual focus for 60–120 seconds** at work distance; **vergence** triggers brainstem **acetylcholine/epinephrine**. For auditory learning, **close your eyes** — visual demand hijacks listening. Don't demand eye contact while someone needs to hear.

items.q: How long should a focused learning bout last?
items.a: Work in **~90-minute ultradian blocks**: warm-up flicker is OK; middle **~1 hour** deep; Wi-Fi off, phone in another room; **re-anchor with the eyes** when attention drifts. Don't demand all-day laser focus.

*"Neuroplasticity doesn't occur during wakefulness, it occurs during sleep."* Acetylcholine **marks synapses** during the day; consolidation is offline. A poor night 1 can still work if **night 2 deep sleep** lands.

items.q: What can accelerate retention right after a session?
items.a: A **~20-minute NSDR** or shallow nap (**≤90 min**) immediately post-learning can **beat waiting for next-night sleep alone** (Cell Reports spatial-memory task). Pair focused bouts with this rest window.
